- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:grill-me: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

+  # The AppImage's own tree, unsandboxed: its ELFs patched to store paths with
+  # autoPatchelf and the binary wrapped with makeWrapper, the way nixpkgs
+  # packages slack or vscode. A patched binary runs on Arch as well as NixOS.
+  # This replaced appimageTools.wrapType2, whose bwrap FHS env everything Orca
+  # spawns (its terminals, the agents in them) inherited: no /etc/hostname,
+  # `date` in UTC (/etc/localtime points into a /usr the env replaced), fonts
+  # dangling, and bwrap between every caller and Electron, forwarding no
+  # signals. tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh.
+  #
+  # Three trees stay byte-identical: what orcad slots are built from, each
+  # file sha256-pinned in resources/orcad-template/orcad-template.json and
+  # checked when a slot is installed -- patched or stripped, the check fails
+  # and Orca downloads stock copies instead. resources/node-runtime's node is
+  # the slot's runtime (pinned by the template's .runtime-node);
+  # resources/orcad-template holds per-target builds (arm64, musl) that Orca
+  # ships to remote hosts; resources/ripgrep is the slots' rg
+  # (packagedRipgrep). All run unpatched on a glibc host with an FHS loader,
+  # which Arch is. The AppImage's own usr/lib (libnotify, libappindicator, ...) is
+  # left out for nixpkgs' copies, below.
+  #
+  # chrome-sandbox ships without the setuid bit (the store cannot hold one);
+  # with unprivileged user namespaces, which Arch has, Chromium uses its
+  # namespace sandbox and never needs it.
+  orcaRuntimeDeps = with pkgs; [
+    libGL systemd libpulseaudio pipewire libva libsecret libnotify
+    libappindicator-gtk3 wayland gtk3
+  ];
+  orca = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation {
+    inherit pname version;
+    src = appimageContents;
+    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.autoPatchelfHook pkgs.makeWrapper ];
+    buildInputs = with pkgs; [
+      alsa-lib at-spi2-atk cairo cups dbus expat glib gtk3 libdrm libgbm
+      libxkbcommon nspr nss pango stdenv.cc.cc.lib systemd
+      libx11 libxcomposite libxdamage libxext libxfixes libxrandr libxcb
+    ];
+    # dlopened, so autoPatchelf cannot see them, and nix's loader has no
+    # /usr/lib to fall back on: GL and udev for the GPU process, pulse and
+    # pipewire for audio and screen capture, libva for video decode,
+    # libsecret for Electron's safeStorage, notify and appindicator for
+    # notifications and the tray; wayland-client and gtk3 for
+    # resources/bin/orca-wayland-clipboard, which links only libc.
+    runtimeDependencies = map lib.getLib orcaRuntimeDeps;
+    dontConfigure = true;
+    dontBuild = true;
+    # Kept off the pinned trees: autoPatchelf by running it by hand below,
+    # strip by not running it at all -- it rewrites the pinned node as surely
+    # as patchelf. installCheckPhase holds the trees to that.
+    dontAutoPatchelf = true;
+    dontStrip = true;
+    installPhase = ''
+      runHook preInstall
+      mkdir -p $out/lib/orca $out/share/applications
+      cp -r --no-preserve=ownership . $out/lib/orca
+      chmod -R u+w $out/lib/orca
+      # AppRun must stay out: Orca's CLI adds --no-sandbox whenever it finds
+      # AppRun beside the executable and `unshare -Ur true` fails (or it runs
+      # as root) -- out/cli/runtime/electron-sandbox-switch.js.
+      rm -r $out/lib/orca/{AppRun,.DirIcon,usr,orca-ide.desktop,orca-ide.png}
+      install -Dm444 orca-ide.desktop $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
       for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
-        install -Dm444 \
-          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
+        install -Dm444 usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
           $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
       done
+      # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
+      # names the app orca-ide, and that is what the desktop Exec and
+      # meta.mainProgram use.
       substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
         --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
+      runHook postInstall
+    '';
+    postFixup = ''
+      targets=()
+      for p in $out/lib/orca/* $out/lib/orca/resources/*; do
+        case $p in
+          */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template|*/resources/ripgrep) ;;
+          *) targets+=("$p") ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      autoPatchelf -- "''${targets[@]}"
+      # runtimeDependencies only reach executables, but Chromium's bundled GL
+      # (ANGLE, SwiftShader) dlopens libEGL/libGL itself, and a dlopen
+      # searches the calling library's RUNPATH. Without this they find GL
+      # only through nixGL's LD_LIBRARY_PATH -- as nixpkgs' electron-bin does.
+      patchelf --add-rpath ${lib.makeLibraryPath orcaRuntimeDeps} \
+        $out/lib/orca/{libEGL.so,libGLESv2.so,libvk_swiftshader.so}
+
+      # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
+      # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and
+      # on a Hyprland-only session there is no X server -- a bare launch exits
+      # 1 with "needs a usable display server". A flag, not an env var, so a
+      # desktop-file launch gets it too. Not in node mode: node rejects it
+      # ("bad option", exit 9), and Orca's CLI probes the app that way
+      # (ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE, with a script as argv).
+      #
+      # FONTCONFIG_FILE: Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly
+      # "DejaVu Sans Mono", which the host's fontconfig lacks; see fontsConf.
+      #
+      # A plain exec: signals and exit codes reach Electron directly.
+      makeWrapper $out/lib/orca/orca-ide $out/bin/orca-ide \
+        --set FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf} \
+        --run '[ -n "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE-}" ] || set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"'
+    '';
+    # Checked where it gates the build. The pinned trees: byte for byte, and
+    # exec bit for exec bit, the AppImage's (fixup's patchShebangs and patchELF still
+    # walk them; today they change nothing), and every pin in orcad's
+    # manifest holding -- ripgrep/* there is resources/ripgrep
+    # (packagedRipgrep). And no way to an unsandboxed Chromium: AppRun gone
+    # (see installPhase), and the desktop Exec exactly the wrapper, no
+    # --no-sandbox carried over from upstream's line.
+    doInstallCheck = true;
+    nativeInstallCheckInputs = [ pkgs.jq ];
+    installCheckPhase = ''
+      runHook preInstallCheck
+      res=$out/lib/orca/resources
+      for d in node-runtime orcad-template ripgrep; do
+        diff -r --no-dereference $src/resources/$d $res/$d
+        # Exec bits and file types; write bits differ by design (chmod u+w).
+        lsx() { (cd $1 && find . \( -perm -u+x -printf 'x %y %p\n' \) -o -printf '- %y %p\n' | sort); }
+        diff <(lsx $src/resources/$d) <(lsx $res/$d)
+      done
+      t=$res/orcad-template
+      jq -r '(.commonSha256 | to_entries[] | "\(.value)  \(.key)"),
+             (.targets | to_entries[] | .key as $t | .value.files | to_entries[]
+               | "\(.value)  targets/\($t)/\(.key)")' $t/orcad-template.json \
+        | while read -r sha p; do
+            f=$t/$p
+            case $p in targets/*/ripgrep/*) [ -e "$f" ] || f=$res/''${p#targets/*/} ;; esac
+            echo "$sha  $f"
+          done | sha256sum -c --quiet

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Cases for the claim that orca.nix runs the Orca GUI unsandboxed: the
     3	# AppImage's tree patched with autoPatchelf and wrapped with makeWrapper, not
     4	# appimageTools' bwrap FHS env.
     5	#
     6	# Why this needs a test. Inside the FHS env, everything Orca spawns -- its
     7	# terminals and the agents in them -- saw the env's /usr, not the host's:
     8	# /etc/hostname was missing, `date` printed UTC (/etc/localtime points into
     9	# /usr/share/zoneinfo), every font fell to Montserrat Thin. And bwrap stood
    10	# between every caller and Electron, forwarding no signals. None of that shows
    11	# from the host, only from a process the app spawns, so these cases probe from
    12	# one.
    13	#
    14	# The probes run on the host. When this script itself runs inside a sandbox
    15	# (an Orca terminal on the old build has no /etc/hostname), each probe goes
    16	# through `systemd-run --user`, whose units the user manager starts outside it.
    17	# Once no bwrap-era Orca is left running anywhere, that path can go.
    18	#
    19	# That the two pinned trees (resources/node-runtime, resources/orcad-template)
    20	# stay the AppImage's byte for byte is the derivation's installCheckPhase, not
    21	# a case here: it gates the build.
    22	#
    23	# The GUI case (5) needs no desktop and never shows on one: it starts its own
    24	# headless sway (wlroots' headless backend, a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) and
    25	# runs Orca in that, with its own --user-data-dir and a throwaway HOME, so it
    26	# never touches a running Orca's profile, ~/.orca/agent-hooks or
    27	# ~/.claude/settings.json. ORCA_TEST_SHOT=<file.png> keeps its screenshot.
    28	#
    29	#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh               build this host's orca and test it
    30	#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh <orca-path>   test a given build, e.g. the live one:
    31	#                                               $(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))
    32	set -u
    33	set -o pipefail
    34	
    35	fails=0; n=0
    36	pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
    37	fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
    38	
    39	FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
    40	
    41	if [ -e /etc/hostname ]; then
    42	  host() { "$@"; }
    43	else
    44	  sr=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$FLAKE" 'nixpkgs#systemd^out') \
    45	    || { echo "inside a sandbox and could not build systemd-run" >&2; exit 1; }
    46	  # Through /bin/sh, so the command is looked up on the host's PATH, not here.
    47	  host() { "$sr/bin/systemd-run" --user --pipe --wait --quiet /bin/sh -c 'exec "$@"' sh "$@"; }
    48	fi
    49	HOSTNAME_=$(host cat /etc/hostname) || { echo "cannot reach the host" >&2; exit 1; }
    50	
    51	ORCA="${1:-}"
    52	if [ -z "$ORCA" ]; then
    53	  drv=$(nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$HOSTNAME_.config.home.packages" \
    54	    --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: builtins.match "orca-[0-9.]+" (p.name or "") != null) ps)).drvPath') \
    55	    || { echo "orca is not in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
    56	  ORCA=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
    57	fi
    58	ORCA=$(readlink -f "$ORCA")
    59	
    60	# The desktop file's Exec names the GUI bin, whatever it is called this week.
    61	# Its arguments, minus field codes (%U), are what case 5 launches with.
    62	read -ra exec_line < <(sed -n 's/^Exec=//p' "$ORCA"/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop | head -1)
    63	exe=${exec_line[0]:-}
    64	exec_args=(); for a in "${exec_line[@]:1}"; do case $a in %*) ;; *) exec_args+=("$a") ;; esac; done
    65	GUI="$ORCA/bin/$exe"
    66	[ -n "$exe" ] && [ -x "$GUI" ] || { echo "no GUI bin from $ORCA's desktop Exec ('$exe')" >&2; exit 1; }
    67	echo "testing $GUI"
    68	
    69	# Under ~/.cache, not /tmp: the bwrap-era sandbox has its own /tmp, which the
    70	# host-side probes would not see.
    71	unit="orca-gui-test-$$"
    72	mkdir -p "$HOME/.cache"
    73	T=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.cache/orca-gui-test.XXXXXX") || { echo "mktemp failed" >&2; exit 1; }
    74	trap 'host systemctl --user stop "$unit" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
    75	
    76	# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.
    77	# grep -c reads it all: -q exits early, and under pipefail nix-store's
    78	# SIGPIPE would send a hit to the else branch.
    79	if [ "$(nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | grep -c -- '-bubblewrap-')" != 0 ]; then
    80	  fail "no sandbox" "bubblewrap is in the closure of $ORCA"
    81	else
    82	  pass "no bubblewrap in the closure"
    83	fi
    84	
    85	# The unwrapped tree: where resources/ lives.
    86	APP=$(nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | while read -r p; do
    87	  [ -f "$p/lib/orca/resources/app.asar" ] && echo "$p/lib/orca"; done | head -1)
    88	[ -n "$APP" ] || { fail "layout" "no lib/orca/resources/app.asar in the closure"; APP=/nonexistent; }
    89	
    90	# 2. Node mode: the wrapper must not inject --ozone-platform, which node
    91	# rejects ("bad option", exit 9). orca's CLI probes the GUI this way.
    92	got=$(host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -p 1 2>&1)
    93	[ "$got" = 1 ] && pass "ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 runs node" \
    94	  || fail "node mode" "printed '$got', want 1"
    95	
    96	# 3. What a spawned process sees is the host: hostname, zone, fonts.
    97	node_run() { # node_run <shell command>: run it from a child of the GUI in node mode
    98	  host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \
    99	    'process.stdout.write(require("child_process").execFileSync("/bin/sh", ["-c", process.argv[1]]))' \
   100	    "$1" 2>&1
   101	}
   102	for c in 'cat /etc/hostname' 'date +%Z' 'readlink /etc/localtime'; do
   103	  want=$(host /bin/sh -c "$c"); got=$(node_run "$c")
   104	  [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "child sees host's '$c' ($want)" \
   105	    || fail "$c" "child got '$got', host has '$want'"
   106	done
   107	# Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono", one
   108	# family with no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another
   109	# mono font; the host has no DejaVu, so orca.nix's fontsConf must apply.
   110	got=$(node_run "fc-list -f '%{family[0]}\n' 'DejaVu Sans Mono' | sort -u | head -1")
   111	[ "$got" = "DejaVu Sans Mono" ] && pass "'DejaVu Sans Mono' exists for the app (terminal default)" \
   112	  || fail "DejaVu" "app's fontconfig has '${got:-nothing}'"
   113	for c in 'sans\-serif:Noto Sans' 'monospace:Noto Sans Mono'; do
   114	  pat=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
   115	  got=$(node_run "fc-match -f '%{family[0]}' '$pat'")
   116	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$pat -> $want for the app" \
   117	    || fail "$pat" "resolves to '${got:-nothing}', want '$want'"
   118	done
   119	
   120	# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty, loaded by this Electron, opens a pty.
   121	got=$(host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
   122	  const p = require(process.argv[1]).spawn("/bin/sh", ["-c", "echo pty-ok"], {});
   123	  let o = ""; p.onData(d => o += d);

This is a READ-ONLY exploration task. You are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from:

Your role is EXCLUSIVELY to search and analyze existing code. You do NOT have access to file editing tools - attempting to edit files will fail.

Your strengths:
- Rapidly finding files using glob patterns
- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns
- Reading and analyzing file contents

- Use Read when you know the specific file path you need to read

Complete the user's search request efficiently and report your findings clearly.

   196	  [ -n "$sock" ] || continue
   197	  in_session "$sway/bin/swaymsg" -s "$sock" -t get_tree > "$T/tree.json" 2>/dev/null || continue
   198	  pid=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
   199	    const walk = n => n.app_id === "orca" ? n.pid : [...n.nodes, ...n.floating_nodes].map(walk).find(Boolean);
   200	    console.log(walk(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1]))) || "");' "$T/tree.json")
   201	  [ -n "$pid" ] && break
   202	done
   203	if [ -z "$pid" ]; then
   204	  fail "window" "no orca window in the headless session after 60s"
   205	  host journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager -n 20
   206	else
   207	  pass "a window maps (pid $pid)"
   208	  # The pid the session launched is the window's: every wrapper execs, so
   209	  # signals and exit codes reach Electron with nothing in between.
   210	  launched=$(cat "$T/orca.pid" 2>/dev/null)
   211	  [ "$launched" = "$pid" ] && pass "the launched pid is Electron's (wrappers exec)" \
   212	    || fail "exec chain" "launched pid '$launched', window pid '$pid'"
   213	  # Give the first frame time, then look at it: a blank or solid surface has
   214	  # a handful of colours, a rendered UI with antialiased text has hundreds.
   215	  sleep 10
   216	  in_session "$grim/bin/grim" -t ppm "$T/shot.ppm"
   217	  colours=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
   218	    const b = require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1]);
   219	    let i = 0, f = 0; const tok = () => { while (/\s/.test(String.fromCharCode(b[i]))) i++;
   220	      const s = i; while (!/\s/.test(String.fromCharCode(b[i]))) i++; return b.slice(s, i).toString(); };
   221	    tok(); tok(); tok(); tok(); i++;
   222	    const seen = new Set(); for (; i + 2 < b.length; i += 3) seen.add((b[i] << 16) | (b[i+1] << 8) | b[i+2]);
   223	    console.log(seen.size);' "$T/shot.ppm" 2>&1)
   224	  [ "${colours:-0}" -gt 100 ] 2>/dev/null && pass "it renders a UI ($colours colours on screen)" \
   225	    || fail "render" "screen has '$colours' colours; blank or broken"
   226	  if [ -n "${ORCA_TEST_SHOT:-}" ]; then in_session "$grim/bin/grim" "$ORCA_TEST_SHOT"; fi
   227	  # The clipboard helper Orca uses on Wayland, against a live compositor.
   228	  got=$(in_session "$APP/resources/bin/orca-wayland-clipboard" --probe 2>&1); rc=$?
   229	  [ "$rc" = 0 ] && pass "orca-wayland-clipboard --probe works in the session" \
   230	    || fail "clipboard" "exit $rc: $got"
   231	  # Chromium's sandbox, with chrome-sandbox left unprivileged: renderers in
   232	  # their own user namespace (layer 1; --no-sandbox renderers share the
   233	  # browser's) and under a seccomp-bpf filter (layer 2, Seccomp: 2).
   234	  ns=$(host /bin/sh -c '
   235	    main=$(readlink /proc/'"$pid"'/ns/user)
   236	    for p in $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup$(systemctl --user show -p ControlGroup --value '"$unit"')/cgroup.procs); do
   237	      tr "\0" " " < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | grep -q -- "--type=renderer" || continue
   238	      [ "$(readlink /proc/$p/ns/user)" != "$main" ] && echo -n userns || echo -n shared-ns
   239	      grep -q "^Seccomp:[[:space:]]*2" /proc/$p/status && echo +seccomp || echo +no-seccomp
   240	    done' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
   241	  [ "$ns" = "userns+seccomp " ] && pass "renderers are sandboxed (own user namespace, seccomp)" \
   242	    || fail "chromium sandbox" "renderers: '${ns:-none}'"
   243	  # SIGTERM to the pid this case started.
   244	  host kill -TERM "$pid"
   245	  for _ in $(seq 20); do [ -s "$T/orca.exit" ] && break; sleep 1; done
   246	  code=$(cat "$T/orca.exit" 2>/dev/null)
   247	  [ "$code" = 0 ] && pass "exits 0 on SIGTERM" || fail "SIGTERM" "exit status '${code:-none after 20s}'"
   248	fi
   249	host systemctl --user stop "$unit" 2>/dev/null
   250	host systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null
   251	# This build's only: a crash of some other Orca meanwhile is not this one's.
   252	cores=$(host coredumpctl list --no-legend --since="@$since" 2>/dev/null | grep -F "$APP" || true)
   253	[ -z "$cores" ] && pass "no coredumps" || fail "coredumps" "$cores"
   254	
   255	printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
   256	[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

I didn't write the findings file. My session runs under a hard read-only rule that bans creating any file, `/tmp` included, and I have no write tool. The full findings are below; to keep the file, save this message to `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-sauyon-orca-workspaces-dotfiles-orca-gui-unsandbox/0f356773-2907-467c-ac73-3e2219018d85/scratchpad/review-r3-correctness.md`.

# Review r3: correctness and error handling (range 39c256fd..HEAD)

The change does what it sets out to do. I found no Critical and no Important issues, only nits.

**State:** `git status` is clean and HEAD is 4b26ec00b56ce6fc0f57e5136b47d26b05828c31. The range is five commits touching the four files you listed.

**What I checked:**
- **Build:** `nix eval` gives `/nix/store/m29zmpq7…-orca-1.4.238`, the nixGL wrapper. It execs `/nix/store/r4nj9cny…-orca-1.4.238/bin/orca-ide`, which:
  - exports `FONTCONFIG_FILE`;
  - runs `[ -n "${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE-}" ] || set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"`;
  - then does a plain `exec` of `lib/orca/orca-ide`.
  - The nixGL script also ends in `exec "$@"`, so every hop execs.
- **Desktop file:** `Exec=orca-ide %U`, and the `MimeType` line includes `x-scheme-handler/orca`.
- **Build log** (`nix log …srqc508c…drv`):
  - `installCheckPhase` really runs, after fixup. It prints `…/node-runtime/bin/node: OK`, and `diff` and `sha256sum --quiet` print nothing.
  - autoPatchelf reports "0 dependencies could not be satisfied". All 10 `runtimeDependencies` reach the executables' RUNPATH.
  - fixup's shrink-rpath and patchShebangs do walk the pinned trees. That changes no bytes there today, and installCheck would catch it if it did.
  - patchShebangs did rewrite `resources/bin/orca-ide` and some `app.asar.unpacked` scripts. These are outside the pinned trees, so that's fine.
- **Manifest coverage:** `orcad-template.json` (schemaVersion 4) holds 255 pins, all 64-hex strings. That equals `commonSha256` plus every `targets[].files` entry, so the jq expression covers every pin.
  - The `targets/*/ripgrep/*` fallback is correct. darwin targets ship ripgrep inside the template, and the linux and win32 ones map to `resources/ripgrep/<arch>/rg`.
- **Error handling:** stdenv phases run with `set -eu -o pipefail`. So a jq failure partway through (say, a target with no `.files`) fails the pipeline even after `sha256sum` passed the lines it got. A missing file fails without `--ignore-missing`, and empty input fails with "no properly formatted lines".
- **Test run:** `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh /nix/store/m29zmpq7…-orca-1.4.238` gave **18/18 passed**. That includes headless sway: window mapped, the launched pid is Electron's, 1034 colours on screen, renderers in their own user namespace with seccomp, exit 0 on SIGTERM.
  - I ran it from inside a bwrap-era sandbox (no `/etc/hostname`), so the `systemd-run --user` path was the one exercised.
  - Afterwards there was no `~/.cache/orca-gui-test.*` left and no `orca-gui-test-*` unit.

## Critical
None.

## Important
None.

## Nits

1. **`orca.nix` (installCheckPhase, `| sha256sum -c --quiet`):** there's no `--strict`.
   - Without it, `sha256sum -c` warns about badly formatted lines and skips them; it only fails when *every* line is bad.
   - Failure scenario: upstream changes some pins to SRI `sha256-…` strings or to objects. `"\(.value)"` then prints lines `sha256sum` can't parse, which are silently skipped, and the build passes with those pins never checked.
   - Impact is limited: `diff -r` against `$src` still enforces byte identity, so this only weakens the "every manifest pin holds" layer. Fix: add `--strict`.
2. **`orca.nix` (installCheckPhase, `lsx` inside `diff <(…) <(…)`):** failures inside a process substitution don't trip `set -e` or `pipefail`.
   - If `cd` or `find` fails on both sides, two empty listings compare equal.
   - Today the `diff -r` just before it would already fail on a missing directory, so this isn't exploitable. Defining `lsx` inside the loop is also redundant.
3. **`orca.nix` (runtime libraries; host-dependent and not exercised by the test):**
   - There's no `wrapGAppsHook3`, so GSettings schemas and gdk-pixbuf loaders come from the host's `XDG_DATA_DIRS`. On shiori, `/usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas` has `org.gtk.Settings.FileChooser`, so a GTK file chooser works. A host without it would abort ("No GSettings schemas") when the GTK picker opens. The portal picker usually takes precedence.
   - The bundled `libvulkan.so.1` will read the host's `/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/intel_icd.json` and dlopen Arch's `libvulkan_intel.so` into a nix-glibc process. Only the non-default Vulkan path uses it.
   - `libpci.so.3` and `libgssapi_krb5.so.2` aren't in `runtimeDependencies`. Chromium tolerates both being missing.
4. **`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:79`:** case 1 can pass when it shouldn't. If `nix-store -qR` fails, `grep -c` still prints `0`, and the case reports "no bubblewrap in the closure". The output isn't checked separately. Low risk, because `$ORCA` was already validated at line 66.
5. **Headless sway isolation (`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:187-191`):** the unit inherits the user manager's environment. Only `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `DISPLAY`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` are unset.
   - `systemctl --user show-environment` also carries `SSH_TPM_AUTH_SOCK`, `GNUPGHOME`, `GPG_TTY`, `BROWSER`, the real `XDG_*_DIR`s, `CARGO_HOME`, `GOPATH` and similar.
   - gpg-agent's socket is under `/run/user/<uid>/gnupg`, which doesn't depend on `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. So a `gpg` call from inside the test instance (for example, signed git in a terminal the app spawns) would reach the live agent, and its pinentry could pop up on the real desktop.
   - The test only launches Orca and spawns nothing like that, so I see no current path onto the desktop. The "no ssh-agent" claim in the comment at line 174 is still only partly true. Consider also unsetting `SSH_TPM_AUTH_SOCK`, `GPG_AGENT_INFO` and `GNUPGHOME`, and setting `GNUPGHOME="$T/home/.gnupg"`.
6. **`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:183`:** `${exec_args[*]}` is spliced unquoted into a sway `exec` string. A `'` in `$T` or `$GUI`, or a desktop-file argument containing spaces, would break it. Nothing does today.
7. **Desktop file coverage:** nothing asserts that `MimeType` keeps `x-scheme-handler/orca`, or that all eight icon sizes exist.
   - Missing icons would fail the build through `install`.
   - The scheme handler isn't checked. If upstream drops it from the desktop file, both the build and the tests still pass.
8. **Font cases (`tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:110-118`):** coverage dropped compared with the deleted `tests/sandbox-fonts.sh`.
   - The old test also checked `sans`, `Arial` and `system-ui` against the host.
   - The probes use the host's `fc-match`, not the app's own fontconfig. That is the same proxy the old test used, but the case names say "for the app".
9. **No direct check of the flag in GUI mode:** no case asserts that `--ozone-platform=wayland` is present outside node mode.
   - If the flag were lost, sway's lazily started Xwayland would give Orca a `DISPLAY`. The window would then map with `app_id` null, and case 5 fails with "no orca window" rather than naming the cause.
   - So the regression is caught, but the failure message points the wrong way.
10. **Stale comments:**
    - `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:19-21` says "two pinned trees (node-runtime, orcad-template)". There are now three, with ripgrep.
    - The label at `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:116` prints `sans\-serif` with the backslash. Cosmetic.

## Would the tests fail on regression?
Yes, for every behaviour you listed. Each item below names what catches it.

| Regression | Caught by |
|---|---|
| bwrap returns | case 1 |
| Flag injected in node mode | case 2 (`-p 1` gets "bad option") |
| `FONTCONFIG_FILE` lost | DejaVu case |
| Lost RUNPATH or missing library | `ld.so --list` and `dlopens` cases |
| Wrapper stops exec'ing | pid-equality case |
| `--no-sandbox` sneaks in | userns+seccomp case |
| `AppRun` or `Exec` line drift | installCheckPhase (build fails) |
| Pinned-tree drift | installCheckPhase `diff -r`, exec-bit diff, `sha256sum` |

The weak spots are nits 1, 4, 7 and 9 above.
